quote: Can I do that now without losing you? Yeah. No. Yeah. You could do that right now.
stewart_read: This is the entry point of the tech-friction spiral. The schema explicitly defines an elderly/low-tech pivot (verbal read-back of kWh numbers) to be used within 2 minutes of friction; the rep instead commits to a live photo-send walkthrough that ultimately consumes about 9 minutes.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer as capable enough to complete the photo send, given he located the bill on his phone unprompted at 04:12 — a reasonable initial bet that only became a miss once friction compounded.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to set an internal 2-minute clock on any bill-navigation struggle and pivot to 'just read me the kWh number off the bill' rather than continuing granular phone instructions.

quote: Yeah. Don't hit the camera. Try to look for something else, like a photos or a, like, a gallery.
stewart_read: Eleven minutes into the same friction point, the rep is still issuing granular UI navigation instructions instead of pivoting to a verbal read-back fallback, confirming this was a sustained miss rather than an isolated stumble.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer had already invested significant effort and was close to success (bill photo was already located), so continuing the photo path may have been the lower-friction choice at this specific late point versus restarting with a verbal read-back.
coaching_implication: Even if continuing made sense at minute 11, the earlier failure to pivot at minute 2-3 is the real coaching moment — flag the total elapsed time against the schema's stated budget.

quote: I may have already done that. I've got it with some some solar outfit, but I'm not sure it was the ion.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior touch with 'some solar outfit' — competitive intelligence the closer would want — and the rep only checks internal records rather than asking which company or what was shown.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been focused on resolving the immediate procedural question (did he already text us this bill) rather than treating it as a sales-intelligence moment, which is a reasonable in-the-moment read but still leaves value on the table.
coaching_implication: Coach a simple follow-up habit: 'Do you remember which company that was, and did you see a design?' costs 15 seconds and arms the closer.

quote: the best way to do it is, you know, a solar field, as I said, just under a a 100 feet from the house.
stewart_read: Customer pushes unsolicited technical/design content (ground-mount solar field placement) a second time; rep correctly declines to engage and redirects to the specialist at 18:09 rather than debating the technical merits.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example worth highlighting to the rep directly — 'They'll talk to you about it, the specialist will talk to you about everything' is the correct universal escape hatch in action.

quote: No. My wife, maybe. I don't know. But
stewart_read: Customer gives an ambiguous answer suggesting his wife may be a co-owner on the title. The rep does not follow up to clarify ownership status and never revisits it when booking the Friday appointment, so a potential co-decider is left off the call entirely.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer's own uncertainty ('I don't know') could be read as the customer self-resolving the question in the negative, making further probing unnecessary — but the schema treats this as a required verify item precisely because customers often don't volunteer clarity unprompted.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close ambiguous ownership answers with a direct clarifying question ('Is she on the title with you?') and, if yes, invite her onto the Friday call per protocols.spouse_decision — this was a clean miss with no follow-up attempt at all.

quote: Okay. Call me back. Put you tomorrow. Put you tomorrow, and then they'll call you at 10AM. Okay? How's that?
stewart_read: The scheduling sequence churns through three different day/time proposals (today at 3PM, tomorrow at 10AM, Friday at 4PM) before landing, reflecting improvisation rather than a clean single offer-and-confirm.
alternative_hypothesis: The churn is customer-driven (he's traveling 200 miles and gives shifting availability), so the rep is reactively adjusting to real constraints rather than failing to anchor — this is the stronger read given the customer's own volunteered travel context at 17:26.
coaching_implication: Once the rep learns the customer won't be home until Friday, jump straight to proposing Friday rather than cycling through today/tomorrow first — saves both the rep and customer time.

quote: I'm a get you all filled out with your estimated design, and then we'll see you on Friday. Okay?
stewart_read: The call closes with a day and time locked (Friday 4PM) and a no-driving condition mentioned, but the rep never states the one-hour block, never uses the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake, and never restates the text-confirmation promise before hanging up.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to run the full button-up checklist even when the call has been long and effortful — the handshake question is a two-second addition that is predictive of show rate.
